chunks: 1169 - And ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī narrated from him:

He was asked about a man who gives the adhan and the iqamah so that he may pray alone, then another man comes and says to him, “Will you pray in congregation?” Is it permissible that they pray with that adhan and iqamah? He said: “No, rather he should give the adhan and iqamah.”

key_terms.الْأَذَانِ: the adhan used for announcing the prayer
key_terms.الْإِقَامَةِ: the iqamah used to begin the prayer
key_terms.يُؤَذِّنُ: he gives the adhan, the call to prayer
key_terms.يُقِيمُ: he gives the iqamah, the call to commence the prayer

ai.seo_question: If someone gave the adhan and iqamah for praying alone, can they use them later for congregational prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the adhan and iqamah when the intention of the prayer changes from individual prayer to congregational prayer. It indicates that the earlier adhan and iqamah given for praying alone are not sufficient for the new congregational setting, and they should be given again.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.1169 - Ammar Al-Sabati narrated that he asked Imam (as) about a man who gives the adhan (call to prayer) and iqamah (call to commence the prayer) intending to pray alone. Then another person arrives and asks to pray in congregation. He asked whether they may use the same adhan and iqamah.
Imam (as) replied: "No, rather he should give the adhan and iqamah again."
